title: The Gift of the Magi
author: O. Henry
plot: Della and Jim are a young married couple with very little money, and it is the day before Christmas. Each secretly wants to buy the other a special gift. Della sells her long beautiful hair to buy a fine chain for Jim's prized pocket watch, while Jim sells his watch to buy lovely combs for Della's hair. When they exchange gifts, both presents are now useless, yet they understand that their love and their willingness to sacrifice for each other are the greatest gift of all.

title: The Last Leaf
author: O. Henry
plot: In a small neighborhood of artists, a young woman named Johnsy falls ill and loses her will to get better. She decides she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy vine on the wall outside her window. Her friend Sue and a gruff old painter named Behrman worry about her through a long, stormy night. In the morning one leaf still clings to the vine, and seeing it survive gives Johnsy hope, and she slowly recovers. Later they learn that kind old Behrman went out in the storm and painted that last leaf on the wall to save her, and that the effort left him ill himself.

title: After Twenty Years
author: O. Henry
plot: Two close friends part in New York and promise to meet again at the same spot in exactly twenty years. On the appointed night, a man waits in a darkened shop doorway and tells a passing policeman about his risky but successful life out west, still loyal to the old promise. Soon another man arrives and greets him, but the waiting man quickly senses something is wrong and that this is not his old friend. It turns out the friendly policeman was Jimmy, his old friend himself, now an officer, who could not bear to arrest him and instead sent a plain-clothes colleague, leaving behind a note that gently explains everything.

title: The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
plot: At Christmas time, Sherlock Holmes examines a battered old hat and a fat goose that a commissionaire brought to him after a street scuffle. Inside the goose he discovers a famous stolen blue gem, the Blue Carbuncle. Holmes cleverly traces the goose backward through a salesman and a market dealer until he finds the real thief, a frightened, trembling man who had hidden the jewel inside the bird. Seeing the man is truly sorry and unlikely to offend again, Holmes decides the Christmas season calls for mercy and lets him go free.

title: The Red-Headed League
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
plot: A red-haired pawnbroker named Mr. Wilson tells Sherlock Holmes about a strange, well-paid job copying an encyclopedia for a club that hires only red-headed men, a club that has now suddenly closed. Holmes realizes the odd job was only a trick to keep Wilson out of his shop for hours each day. The true plan is a secret tunnel being dug from Wilson's cellar toward the vault of a bank next door. Holmes, the police, and the bank wait quietly in the vault at night and catch the clever criminal in the act, without anyone being harmed.

title: The Ransom of Red Chief
author: O. Henry
plot: Two men who are short of money kidnap the young son of a wealthy townsman, expecting an easy ransom. But the boy, who happily calls himself Red Chief, is so wild and full of games that he torments his two captors day and night and has no wish to go home at all. Worn out, the kidnappers keep lowering their ransom demand just to get rid of him. In the end the boy's clever father agrees to take his son back only if the men pay HIM, and the two exhausted kidnappers gladly hand over the money to be free of the boy.

title: The Bremen Town Musicians
author: Brothers Grimm
plot: An old donkey, no longer wanted by his master, sets off to become a musician in the town of Bremen. Along the way he meets a tired dog, an old cat, and a rooster, each cast aside because of age, and they decide to travel together. At night in the forest they come upon a cottage full of robbers eating a feast. By climbing on one another's backs and making a sudden, terrible noise, the four animals frighten the robbers away and take the cozy cottage for themselves. They enjoy it so much that they never reach Bremen and instead live happily together for the rest of their days.

title: The Elephant's Child
author: Rudyard Kipling
plot: Long ago, elephants had no trunks, only small bulgy noses. One young elephant is endlessly curious and asks so many questions that the other animals are tired of him, especially his question about what the crocodile eats for dinner. Full of curiosity, he travels to the great grey-green river to find out for himself, and the crocodile seizes his little nose and pulls hard. In the long tug-of-war his nose stretches and stretches into a long trunk, which turns out to be marvelously useful for eating, drinking, and swatting flies. When he returns home, all the other elephants soon want long trunks of their own.

title: Rikki-Tikki-Tavi
author: Rudyard Kipling
plot: A young mongoose named Rikki-Tikki is swept by a flood into the garden of a kind English family, who dry him off and take him in. Exploring the garden, he learns that two dangerous cobras, Nag and Nagaina, rule it and threaten the family and the other small creatures. Brave and quick, Rikki-Tikki decides to protect his new home. Through courage and cleverness he outwits both cobras and finds Nagaina's last hidden egg, ending their reign. The garden is peaceful again, and proud Rikki-Tikki keeps watch over the family he has come to love.

title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
author: Washington Irving
plot: In a quiet, dreamy village famous for its ghost tales, a tall and timid schoolmaster named Ichabod Crane hopes to marry pretty Katrina and win her family's rich farm. His cheerful rival, Brom Bones, plays pranks to scare him away. Riding home alone on a dark night after a lively party, Ichabod is chased through the woods by a terrifying figure that seems to be the legendary Headless Horseman. By morning Ichabod has vanished from the village, leaving only his hat and a smashed pumpkin behind. The townspeople never learn for certain whether it was a real ghost or bold Brom in disguise, and Ichabod is never seen there again.

title: The Cop and the Anthem
author: O. Henry
plot: On a cold autumn night, a homeless old man named Soapy decides he wants to be arrested so he can spend the freezing winter warm and fed in a comfortable jail. He tries one small scheme after another to get himself caught, but every clumsy attempt comically fails and no policeman will take him. At last, standing outside a church and hearing beautiful organ music drift out, he is deeply moved and resolves to turn his life around and find honest work. At that very moment, ironically, a policeman finally arrests him for loitering.

title: The Celebrated Jumping Frog
author: Mark Twain
plot: A long-winded old man tells the narrator the tale of Jim Smiley, a fellow who would bet on absolutely anything. Smiley catches a frog named Dan'l Webster and trains it until it can out-jump any frog around. A clever stranger accepts Smiley's bet, then secretly fills the frog with lead shot while Smiley goes off to catch a frog for the stranger to use. Weighed down, poor Dan'l cannot jump at all, the stranger wins the bet and strolls away, and only afterward does a puzzled Smiley discover the trick that beat him.

title: The Open Road
author: Kenneth Grahame
plot: Mole and his friend Water Rat go to visit the wealthy, excitable Mr. Toad, who has grown bored of boats and fallen in love with a gaily painted gypsy caravan. Toad happily persuades the two friends to take to the open road with him, and they set off with a horse and cart, camping and singing along the way. All is merry until a roaring motor-car speeds past, frightens their horse, and tips the little cart into a ditch. Rather than being upset, Toad sits in the road utterly enchanted, and from that moment he can think of nothing but owning a motor-car of his own, hinting at the mischief still to come.

title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
author: Beatrix Potter
plot: Mother Rabbit warns her four children not to go into Mr. McGregor's garden, then leaves to do her shopping. The three good little rabbits gather blackberries, but naughty Peter squeezes under the gate and stuffs himself with lettuces and radishes. Mr. McGregor spots him and gives chase, and Peter, terrified, loses his little blue jacket and shoes as he struggles to escape. At last he wriggles free and races home, worn out and frightened, and is put to bed with a spoonful of chamomile tea while his obedient sisters enjoy a fine supper of bread, milk, and blackberries.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
plot: In a London gentlemen's club, the calm and precise Phileas Fogg wagers a large sum that he can travel all the way around the world in just eighty days. With his lively new French servant Passepartout, he sets off at once by train and steamship, crossing many countries and facing storms, missed connections, and unexpected delays. A detective who wrongly believes Fogg is a fleeing bank robber follows him and causes further trouble. Racing against the clock and helping a kind traveler named Aouda along the way, Fogg presses steadily on, and thanks to his cleverness and a lucky mistake about the calendar, he arrives back in London and wins his bet at the very last second.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare
author: Aesop
plot: A speedy hare loves to boast and laughs at a slow-moving tortoise for being so slow. Tired of the teasing, the tortoise calmly challenges the hare to a race, and all the animals gather to watch. The hare dashes far ahead and, certain he cannot possibly lose, lies down for a lazy nap by the roadside. The steady tortoise never stops, plodding on and on, and quietly passes the sleeping hare. The hare wakes too late and can only watch the tortoise cross the finish line first, learning that slow and steady wins the race.

title: The Lion and the Mouse
author: Aesop
plot: A mighty lion is dozing in the sun when a tiny mouse accidentally scampers across his paws and wakes him. The angry lion catches the little mouse, but is so amused by its desperate plea that he lets it go free; the grateful mouse promises that one day it will repay the kindness, and the lion laughs at the very idea. Some time later, the lion is caught fast in a hunter's strong rope net and cannot break free no matter how he struggles. Hearing the lion's roars, the little mouse hurries over and gnaws through the ropes with its sharp teeth, setting the great lion free and proving that even the smallest friend can help the strongest.

title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
author: Aesop
plot: A young shepherd boy is bored while watching his flock of sheep on a lonely hillside, so for fun he shouts that a wolf is attacking. The villagers drop their work and rush up the hill to help, only to find no wolf and a laughing boy; annoyed, they trudge back down, and the boy plays the same trick a second time. Later a real wolf truly does appear among the sheep, and the boy cries out for help with all his might. But the villagers, sure it is another lie, ignore his shouts and stay in the village. The boy learns the hard way that no one believes a liar, even when he is finally telling the truth.

title: The Selfish Giant
author: Oscar Wilde
plot: A giant returns home after a long absence and is angry to find children playing in his beautiful garden, so he builds a high wall and puts up a sign to keep everyone out. But then his garden falls under an endless winter of frost and snow, while spring blooms everywhere else in the land. One day the children slip back in through a small gap, and wherever they go spring returns, and the giant finally understands that his own selfishness caused the long winter. Filled with regret, he tears down the wall and shares his garden with the children forever after, becoming gentle and dearly loved, and finds true happiness at last.

title: The Ugly Duckling
author: Hans Christian Andersen
plot: On a farm one summer, a large and awkward duckling hatches among the others and is teased and pecked for looking different from everyone around him. Lonely and unhappy, he wanders away from the farm and survives a long, hard, cold winter all on his own. When spring finally arrives, he sees a flock of magnificent white swans gliding on the water and, expecting to be chased away, sadly bows his head. But in his reflection he discovers that he has grown into a beautiful swan himself, and the other swans welcome him warmly, and he is happier than he ever dared to dream.

title: The Emperor's New Clothes
author: Hans Christian Andersen
plot: A vain emperor who cares about nothing but fine clothes is visited by two swindlers pretending to be master weavers. They claim to weave a magical cloth that is invisible to anyone who is stupid or unfit for their job, and, afraid to seem foolish, the emperor and all his ministers pretend to admire the cloth that does not really exist. The emperor then parades proudly through the town in his splendid 'new clothes,' and the crowd, not wanting to look silly, pretends to admire them too. Suddenly a small child cries out that the emperor is wearing nothing at all, the truth spreads through the crowd, and the red-faced emperor realizes he has been tricked.

title: The Elves and the Shoemaker
author: Brothers Grimm
plot: A poor but honest shoemaker has only enough leather left for one last pair of shoes, so he cuts the pieces out and leaves them on his bench to sew in the morning. When he wakes, he finds the shoes finished perfectly, and they sell so well that he can buy more leather; night after night the same wonderful thing keeps happening and he begins to prosper. Curious to know his helper, the shoemaker and his wife hide one night and watch, and they see two tiny bare elves stitching busily until dawn. To thank them, the grateful couple secretly make the elves little clothes and shoes, and the delighted elves dance merrily away and, their work done, are never seen again.

title: How the Camel Got His Hump
author: Rudyard Kipling
plot: At the very beginning of the world, when the animals had just begun to work for man, a lazy camel lives alone in the middle of a desert and refuses to do any work at all, answering every request with a rude 'Humph!' The horse, the dog, and the ox grow angry because they must do the idle camel's share of the work as well as their own. A powerful Djinn who is in charge of all deserts hears their complaint and goes to speak with the camel, who only says 'Humph!' once again. As a fitting punishment, the Djinn magically gives the camel a great humph, a hump, upon his back, so that he can work for three days without eating, and camels have carried their humps ever since.

title: Rip Van Winkle
author: Washington Irving
plot: Rip Van Winkle is a friendly, good-natured but lazy man who, to escape his sharp-tongued wife, wanders up into the mountains one day with his dog and his gun. There he meets a group of strange little men in old-fashioned clothes playing a game of ninepins, shares a drink from their keg, and falls into a deep, deep sleep. When he wakes, his gun has rusted, his beard has grown long, and his dog is gone; returning to his village he finds that twenty whole years have passed and everything has changed. Confused and amazed, Rip is at last recognized by a few old neighbors, tells his astonishing tale, and happily lives out his remaining years as the village's most beloved old storyteller.

title: Puss in Boots
author: Charles Perrault
plot: A poor miller dies and leaves his youngest son nothing but a clever cat, which seems a very small inheritance. But the cat asks only for a pair of boots and a sack, and then, through cunning tricks, begins bringing fine gifts to the king in the name of his master, whom he grandly calls the 'Marquis of Carabas.' The cat arranges for the king to meet his master and then outwits a rich ogre by daring it to turn itself into a tiny mouse, which the cat instantly pounces on, winning the ogre's great castle. Delighted by the charming 'marquis' and his lands, the king happily gives him the princess in marriage, and the cat becomes a grand lord who need never chase mice again except for his own amusement.

title: The Three Questions
author: Leo Tolstoy
plot: A king becomes convinced that he would never fail at anything if only he knew the answers to three questions: what is the right time to begin each thing, who are the most important people, and what is the most important thing to do. No one at court can answer to his satisfaction, so he disguises himself and visits a wise old hermit who lives simply, digging his garden in the hills. While the king is there, a hurt and exhausted stranger stumbles out of the woods, and the king spends the day caring for him; the stranger turns out to have been an enemy who came to harm the king but now becomes a grateful friend. Through these simple events the hermit shows the king the answers: the most important time is now, the most important person is the one you are with, and the most important thing is to do that person good.
